item.title: Undoing a Correction Without Losing What Came After
item.description: One translation fixed the early trajectory and ruined the late one. How long a navigation correction should live, how to tell it has gone stale, and why undoing it means keeping a fallback that keeps updating.

item.title: Splitting Prefill from Decode: What DistServe Buys and Costs
item.description: Prefill and decode share weights but not shapes, so running them together slows both. How DistServe sizes two GPU pools, what moving KV between them costs, and what the paper measured.

item.title: Held-Out Data That Isn't Independent
item.description: Holding out later observations is the right instinct, but in navigation every segment shares the same inertial, map and device errors. How to freeze a candidate correction and still score it honestly.

item.title: Six TensorRT Engines from One Linear Layer
item.description: One MatMul → Add → Relu graph, built six ways in FP32 and FP16. Which shapes each engine accepts, where FP16 overflows, and what a reused execution context really costs per call.

item.title: When a Sparse Autoencoder Reconstructs Better and Finds Less
item.description: On data with 12 known directions, letting each sample use 4 latents instead of 2 lowered an SAE's reconstruction error and halved the directions it recovered. Reconstruction isn't explanation.

item.title: How a First-Order Rotation Stretched an 18 m Walk to 25 m
item.description: A correction cut reference error from 24.5 m to 4.8 m and made the route 40% longer. Why a large first-order rotation also scales, checked on all 146 trajectory edges, and how relinearizing fixes it.

item.title: Where TVM's Fusion Stops
item.description: Two matmuls became one and five functions became two, yet three temporary matrices survived. Following one Relax program down to TIR loops to see what TVM's fusion actually removed.

item.title: Why a Perfect Magnetometer Fit Says Nothing About Direction
item.description: Ellipsoid calibration fixes each reading's length, so any rotation of a valid calibration fits equally well. The rotation gauge, when planar motion starves heading, and a real column-order bug in the logs.

item.title: CUDA Graphs Save Launches, Not Work
item.description: A graph cut a four-kernel attention chain from 33 μs to 12 μs on the GPU, yet the smallest full request got slower. What capture saves, what it binds, and when replay pays off.

item.title: What Marginalization Remembers, Including the Mistakes
item.description: Marginalization keeps old constraints after old states are dropped, wrong ones included. Schur and QR from a hand-solvable example, 700 replayed propagations, and what a sliding window costs.

item.title: Ignoring Cross-Covariance Turned a Pause into a 7 m/s Sprint
item.description: Same observations, two answers: with the full common source a standing person moves at 0.18 m/s; treat motion edges as independent and it's 7 m/s. The mechanism, the ablation and the diagnostics.

item.title: Swapping Gaussian for Student-t Changes More Than the Tail
item.description: Hand a Gaussian's Q to a Student-t with 4 degrees of freedom and its covariance doubles. Scale, central pull and tail all change at once; untangling which one moved a robust WiFi solution, failures included.

item.title: When Two Estimators Share One Observation
item.description: Giving a heading estimator first call on WiFi fixes cut the position filter's accepted fixes from 42 to 7 and never produced a heading correction. Shared evidence needs ownership, not just an order.

item.title: When a Denser WiFi Map Gives Worse Answers
item.description: A fingerprint map grew from 1,022 to 4,852 synthetic points and matched fewer queries. The old points weren't better; they claimed to hear all 1,045 APs. Three ways to densify a map, and the error each brings.

item.title: How an Attention Head Says Nothing: Sinks and Output Gates
item.description: Softmax makes every head output a weighted average, so a head can't scale itself down. A zero-value sink or an output gate fixes that; StreamingLLM, Qwen's gating, and when the two are equivalent.

item.title: When Removing Bank Conflicts Made My GEMM Slower
item.description: An XOR swizzle took shared-memory bank conflicts on a 1024³ FP32 GEMM to zero and made the kernel 19.5% slower. Bank addressing, double buffering and cp.async, and where the time went.

item.title: What Quantizing the KV Cache Costs in Speed and Accuracy
item.description: Fewer bytes per key don't guarantee faster attention: decoding, addressing and reductions can hand the savings back. One INT8 decode step measured, then how absmax, rotation and QJL change attention.

item.title: Online Softmax in CUDA: No Score Matrix, More Time
item.description: Skipping the 16 MiB score matrix for 2048-token attention should be a win, yet the online kernel ran slower. Deriving the online state, the CUDA kernel and its bugs, and why the cost sits outside the formula.

item.title: Where a Naive CUDA GEMM Loses 5× to cuBLAS
item.description: One output per thread took 3.26 ms on a 1024³ matrix; cuBLAS took 0.62 ms. Block tiling, register outer products and float4 loads, checked in SASS and measured across square, skinny and short-K shapes.

item.title: A Custom SwiGLU Op in PyTorch: Everything but the Kernel
item.description: The SwiGLU kernel is one sigmoid and one multiply. Shipping it means handling offset views, the current stream, autograd and FakeTensor, each of which can break it on its own.

item.title: Where TF32 Loses Precision, and What It Buys Back
item.description: TF32 keeps FP32's range but sends 11 bits into the multiply. A dot product you can check by hand, the RNA rounding rule, error split against two FP64 references, and whether two WMMA kernels are faster.

item.title: Megatron vs. FSDP, Derived from a Two-Layer MLP
item.description: A 7B model's training state is 104 GiB on its own. Shard the state or shard the computation: deriving what tensor parallelism and FSDP each save and where their communication comes from.

item.title: Why Hierarchical AllReduce Isn't 8× Faster
item.description: Sending one-eighth of each gradient off-node doesn't help if all eight eighths leave through the same network card. Following one gradient, then the bytes, through BlueConnect, TACCL and multi-port rings.

item.title: From CoT to SCoRe: What Each Method Actually Supervises
item.description: Two solutions reach x = 8, one by luck. Following them through CoT, sampling, STaR, process and outcome rewards, and SCoRe shows what each method rewards and what it can't see.

item.title: Why the Scaling-Law Training Recipe Keeps Changing
item.description: Training 7B on 140B tokens costs about what 70B on 14B does. Kaplan vs. Chinchilla, repeated data, serving cost and inference-time compute each change which one you should train.

item.title: Why a Serial Loop Beat My Parallel Selective Scans
item.description: A plain time-serial kernel was fastest in 11 of 12 shapes on an RTX 5070 Laptop, up to 24× ahead of the parallel scans. Only the narrowest state, N=32, let a chunked scan win.

item.title: Right Floor, Wrong Height: A Barometer in Indoor Navigation
item.description: All 848 reference points had the right floor, while one route's height spanned 20 m without changing floors. How pressure became continuous height inside the shared filter, and what each fix cost.
